newsitem.title: UK: Iraqi oil export delay pushes crude price upward.
newsitem.headline: Iraqi oil export delay pushes crude price upward.

text.p: World oil prices firmed on Monday after Iraq indicated it would take longer than first thought to restart its exports of crude.
Iraqi envoy Abdul Amir al-Anbari said that he did not anticipate Baghdad restarting crude flows until August.
The market had foreseen an early to mid-July date after Iraqi oil minister Amir Muhammed Rasheed last week predicted quick agreement with the United Nations on an aid distribution plan.

The aid is bound for Iraq under the terms of an oil-for-food accord struck in December. The first six-month deal, allowing $2.14 billion worth of oil sales, expired in early June and was renewed by the Security Council.
But disputes between the U.N. and Baghdad over the signing of aid contracts have held up fresh crude flows, tightening supplies for the world's oil markets.

By 1513 GMT, August futures for international benchmark Brent blend crude oil were up 18 cents at $18.36 a barrel in London, while in New York front-month West Texas Intermediate contracts were up 14 cents at $19.60.
"It would take about a month for the new resolution to be implemented, including the oil sales," Anbari told Reuters in an interview in Geneva on Monday.
"I think end of July, beginning of August, the new resolution would come into force...If all goes well, we'd resume sales in early August," he said.

His time-frame was more pessimistic than Rasheed's but more in line with the expectations of the market, which thought bureaucratic and logistical obstacles would prevent oil liftings much before mid-July.

The gradual realisation that no Iraqi barrels will be available for some weeks from the load-ports of Ceyhan in Turkey and the Mina al-Bakr terminal in the Gulf has forced buyers to cover needs well in advance.
They have scrambled for Russian Urals cargoes, the nearest direct alternative to Iraqi "sour," or high sulphur, crude in the Mediterranean.
And in the North Sea an overspill of buying pressure has pushed values higher, clearing out most crude cargoes scheduled for July well in advance of what would be normal.
Brent crude prices have recovered from a 15-month low hit on June 11 and are now around $18 a barrel.
But some traders discounted Anbari's statement, suggesting that although he negotiated the oil-for-food accord last year he was no longer attuned to events.
Deputy prime minister Tareq Aziz said on Sunday Iraq had already finalised its aid distribution plan and was waiting for a U.N. team to travel to Baghdad to approve it.
Iraq will have to export a hefty million barrels a day once technicalities are ironed out if is to hit its cash target, flooding markets with surplus oil that will depress prices.
The oil deluge will undo what little support for prices the Organisation of the Petroleum Exporting Countries secured last week at its Vienna meeting.
Gulf states in the 11-nation cartel pressured quota-busting members to restrain rampant production, but observers were sceptical cut-backs could be secured.
